blacklistabilityReview.evidence: cgUSD has a direct but non-targeted control surface. The verified CgUSD contract at 0xca72827a3d211cfd8f6b00ac98824872b72cab49 on Base exposes pause() and resume() as onlyOwner functions, and inherited StToken._transferShares() calls _requireNotPaused(), so the owner can stop ordinary token and share transfers globally. At Base block 52800750, owner() is 0xfecab866b450b97db38500898e9272c1d18918b7 (a contract without Safe getThreshold/getOwners methods) and paused() is false. The ABI contains no blacklist, freeze, seize, forced-transfer or arbitrary-holder burn function, so the issuer cannot target an individual holder. A global transfer pause is a direct Possible control, not a Yes blacklist. There is no declared parent; reserve composition (Treasury bills plus an undisclosed on-chain stablecoin portfolio) is not measured and does not decide the verdict.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: cgUSD has one tracked Base deployment: a direct, non-proxy rebasing token administered by a TimelockController (10-second delay, 2-of-11 Safe proposer). Native minting takes the token's configured USDC asset. Issuer docs describe Axelar communication for deposits from other chains, with cgUSD existing solely on Base; no satellite cgUSD representation is authored here.

routes.reviewNote: At Base block 52024130 on 2026-10-01, cgUSD owner() is 0xfecab866b450b97db38500898e9272c1d18918b7, asset() is native Base USDC 0x833589fcd6edb6e08f4c7c32d4f71b54bda02913, and the correct EIP-1967 implementation and admin slots are zero. Verified CgUSD source implements mint(address,uint256) and StToken share accounting rather than ERC-4626. The issuer mint page states cgUSD exists solely on Base and uses Axelar for cross-chain deposit communication.
